decision.reason: The primitive hexagonal cell and Z=2 are strongly fixed by all reproducible peak positions and systematic absences, and the submitted P6_3/mmc ZrBeSi-type framework is chemically plausible (including 2.237 A Cu-S contacts). The trajectory explicitly compared all six Li/Cu/S assignments on the 2a/2c/2d orbits; only Li on 2a matches the dominant intensities, while swapping Cu and S between 2c and 2d is merely an origin-equivalent description, not a distinct ordering ambiguity. A lower-symmetry P6_3mc coordinate refinement produced only a marginal improvement and retained essentially the same Cu/S layer relation. Although no comparable Rwp was supplied, an independent intensity check with wavelength-appropriate Cu Kalpha anomalous scattering and a single isotropic displacement factor reconciles the apparent odd-l suppression and gives about 1.9% normalized RMS error in integrated intensities, with every reproducible line accounted for. Thus the submitted symmetry, ideal coordinates, full occupancies, and element ordering are sufficiently established, and no materially different scientifically motivated candidate is likely to improve the set.

The submitted Fm-3m model is sufficiently established. The meaningful reflections consistently index the F-centered cubic cell (a about 11.184 A), and the explicit Y(8c)+Ga(24d)+Ga(24e) model with x about 0.19533 closely reproduces the observed peak positions and the full extracted intensity sequence. The trajectory instantiated the principal composition-preserving alternative Y/Ga Wyckoff decompositions, which fit decisively worse, while the selected model has plausible density and interatomic distances. The two framework sites contain the same element, so no unresolved Ga ordering remains. Although no comparable whole-pattern report was supplied, the direct profile and reflection-level evidence is not dubious and gives no scientifically motivated materially different survivor warranting another attempt.

The submitted model is sufficiently established. The indexed approximately 244.68 A^3 perovskite cell accounts for the observed peak positions, and the explicit Z=1 SrPr3Fe4O12 realization gives a strong whole-pattern fit (trace-reported unweighted Rwp about 5.5%) with sensible fully occupied stoichiometry and Fe-O distances. Crucially, the trajectory did not merely assume or average the 1:3 A-site order: it instantiated all four Sr placements, reducing to two powder-distinct cases, and the alternative ordering fit measurably worse while the tied placement is inversion-equivalent. Monoclinic/orthorhombic metrics and additional coordinate freedom were also tested; the refined weakly triclinic metric improved the fit, whereas unconstrained lower-symmetry coordinates produced chemically implausible bond distortions. Although no external comparable-Rwp score was supplied, the trace provides adequate support for the cell, framework, explicit ordering, metric symmetry, and constrained coordinates, with no scientifically credible materially different survivor warranting another attempt.

The submission is sufficiently established for exact-recovery stopping. All 25 credible reflections index on one A-centered orthorhombic cell (V about 111.06 A^3) with very high indexing figures of merit, and Z=2 gives a plausible 10.70 g/cm^3 Tb-rich phase. The ordered Amm2 model accounts for the observed peak positions and intensities across 5-90 degrees with a low integrated-intensity residual (R2 about 0.0032), including weak reflections and systematic absences; its Tb-Si/C and Si-C distances are physically reasonable. The trajectory explicitly rejected centrosymmetric Cmmm and incompatible Cmm2 decorations, searched a centered lower-symmetry model, and enumerated all 2a/2b assignments for two Tb, Si, and C sites. The four equal best Amm2 minima are not distinct element orderings: origin shifts/inversion plus relabeling the indistinguishable Tb sites transform them into the submitted realization. The nearest numerically competing assignment places Si and C essentially on top of one another and is physically inadmissible, while the remaining assignments fit far worse. Although no separate comparable-Rwp report was supplied, the available whole-pattern and trajectory evidence supports the cell, Z, Amm2 framework, coordinates, full occupancies, and element ordering without a surviving material discrete ambiguity.

The tetragonal metric cell and I-centering are well supported, and Z=12 is density-plausible, but the submitted exact structure is not established. The final CIF is a P1 realization with 30 independent sites plus exact centering; spglib finds no rotational symmetry even at 1.0 A tolerance, despite the trajectory first asserting I41/acd and exploring several other tetragonal groups. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp is available. The reported 0.952 score is only a stick-intensity cosine; a direct profile reconstruction still has about 0.30 relative unweighted residual and the trace lists appreciable calculated reflections absent from the observation. The geometry is also irregular, including S-Cl contacts near 1.89-1.94 A, Cd-Cd near 2.40 A, and strongly inconsistent coordination environments. Most importantly, the coordinates and element ordering came from one charge-flip map followed by unconstrained P1 refinement and discrete reassignment; multiple nearby map/order/refinement outcomes were produced but not preserved and rigorously compared as candidate structures. Thus the data support the cell and perhaps a coarse average framework, not the submitted symmetry, coordinates, or unique Cd/Sb/S/Cl ordering, and materially different symmetry-constrained or ordering alternatives could plausibly improve the candidate set.

The body-centered tetragonal cell (a about 10.167 A, c about 4.764 A), Z=8, and a plausible Li-Cu-S average framework are well supported, but the exact submitted I4/mmm realization is not. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the trajectory's own calculated intensities show material discrepancies at multiple strong reflections (for example 24.75, 32.39, 47.45, and 48.65 degrees 2theta). The selected coordinates came from a custom integrated-intensity objective; a separate profile fit moved Li appreciably, demonstrating that its coordinate is weakly constrained, and a locally relaxed I-4 model improved that objective without a rigorous whole-pattern or significance comparison. The search did not instantiate and compare a sufficiently broad set of lower-symmetry/order-distinct periodic alternatives. Thus physical plausibility and cell recovery do not establish the submitted symmetry, exact coordinates, and Li ordering, and another scientifically motivated attempt is warranted.

The primitive triclinic cell and Z=1 are strongly supported by peak positions (62 mapped peaks with about 0.008 degrees 2theta RMS), but the submitted exact structure is not sufficiently established. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied, and the trajectory's instantiated full-profile oxygen models remained poor at roughly Rwp=0.37-0.46; the final P-1 coordinates were instead selected by fitting only 21 extracted low-angle reflection intensities, with large residual intensity errors and unstable allocation within unresolved reflection groups. The trace also found a materially different V sublattice that fit the high-angle intensity proxy substantially better (objective about 0.308 versus 0.465 for the submitted V framework) but never instantiated and whole-pattern-compared it with oxygen models. Multiple distinct oxygen-coordinate basins had similar objectives, while the selected geometry still contains unusually short V-O contacts near 1.50 angstrom and was chosen through an explicit fit-versus-contact penalty tradeoff. Thus the cell/Z are credible, but the submitted P-1 V/O coordinates, coordination framework, and oxygen ordering are not uniquely supported; another attempt with true whole-pattern refinement and explicit comparison of the surviving V/O frameworks is warranted.

The candidate is sufficiently established for exact-recovery purposes. The primitive trigonal cell indexes every substantive reflection (reported peak-position RMS 0.00118 degrees 2theta), and the submitted ideal three-layer perovskite reproduces the observed intensities across 5-90 degrees; an independent profile reconstruction gives an approximately 4.1% unweighted whole-pattern residual despite the comparable-Rwp report being unavailable. The trace instantiated all 120 assignments of Ba, La, Mg, and Fe over the three framework A and three B sites: every best model places Ba/La/Mg on the A sublattice and Fe on the B sublattice, while the next assignment class has about four times the log-intensity error. The C-centered monoclinic cell and approximately Z=4 are strongly supported by indexing, and the density/formula are plausible, but the submitted exact C2 realization is not established. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and independent profile checking shows large intensity errors (for example, the calculated 23.98 and 27.88 degree peaks are about half the observed relative intensities, while the 35.87 degree peak is about twice the observed intensity); the selected cell also leaves k-bearing reflections shifted by up to about 0.03 degree after the trace identified a d-spacing bug. The trajectory ended during correction/refinement, produced no final response, and did not resolve element ordering or lower-symmetry/alternative coordinate models with a physically constrained conventional whole-pattern refinement. Another solution attempt is warranted.

The ordered model systematically overpredicts the odd-l ordering reflections (e.g. observed integrated 101 intensity about 29.5 versus calculated 41.8, with similar deficits for 103, 201, 203, 211, and 213), and no comparable whole-pattern Rwp is available. The intensity fit sharply supports Y on 8c with Ga on 24d and 24e (x about 0.19533); the trace instantiated and compared materially different 56-atom Y/Ga site decompositions, which fit substantially worse, while the published tetragonal YGa6 structure has an incompatible lattice and reflection geometry. The CIF round-trips as fully occupied YGa6 with Z = 8 and has plausible Y-Ga and Ga-Ga contacts. The indexed approximately 244.68 A^3 cell, Z=1 composition cell, average perovskite framework, and Fe-O geometry are credible, but exact structure recovery is not sufficiently established. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied, and the trajectory's best self-reported unweighted profile Rwp is about 0.0548 (about 0.0572 for the selected CIF in the preceding check), versus its own estimated noise-limited value of about 0.0257, with remaining intensity mismatches. Thus the diffraction supports the cell and average framework much more strongly than the submitted symmetry, exact coordinates, and element ordering, and another scientifically motivated solution attempt could plausibly improve or expand the candidate set.

The candidate is sufficiently established despite the unavailable comparable-Rwp report. The tetragonal metric cell and I-centered reflection lattice are well supported, but the submitted exact structure is not. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and an independent profile fit of the CIF (with optimized scale, zero shift, peak width, background, and isotropic damping) still gives an approximately 0.30 normalized profile residual; the reported 0.952 stick cosine also masks major relative-intensity errors and calculated peaks absent from the data. Physical plausibility is also poor: the model contains 1.88 A S-S, 1.89-1.94 A S-Cl, and 2.06 A Cd-S contacts, with strongly irregular/undercoordinated Cd environments. A scientifically motivated search in the supported I-centered tetragonal lattice, with explicit symmetry/Z and element-ordering alternatives and genuine whole-profile comparison, could materially improve the candidate set.

The I-centered tetragonal cell is convincingly indexed and the submitted I4/mmm model is chemically plausible, so the cell and average Cu-S framework have substantial support. The trajectory also searched a restricted family dominated by one multiplicity-8 Wyckoff orbit per element; it did not materially instantiate and compare split-orbit realizations, alternative Z/orderings, or broader subgroup models. Li is especially weakly constrained: its intensity objective is shallow and its coordinate moved from about 0.357 to 0.351 in the attempted full-profile fit. Round-trip symmetry checks cannot resolve those structural ambiguities. A further attempt using proper whole-pattern refinement and explicit chemically plausible symmetry/ordering alternatives could materially improve the candidate set.

The indexed triclinic cell is strongly supported and Z = 1 is chemically plausible, but the exact submitted P-1 realization is not established. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied; the trace's own profile refinements remained poor (Rwp about 0.37-0.38), and an independent simple whole-profile check also showed substantial disagreement, especially at higher angles. The model is chemically problematic: several V-O contacts are about 1.499 A, the inversion-center V is severely underbonded (bond-valence sum about 2.1 versus the required average V oxidation state of +4.8), other V sites are strongly overbonded, and automated valence assignment fails. The trajectory imposed centrosymmetry and encountered many distinct oxygen solutions but did not instantiate and compare materially different P1/P-1 coordinate or framework alternatives. Thus the cell and perhaps part of the V sublattice are supported, whereas the symmetry and atomic coordinates are not, and another structure-solution attempt is scientifically warranted.

The C-centered monoclinic cell (approximately a=6.784, b=7.424, c=6.401 A, beta=92.716 degrees) and a plausible Z=4 are strongly supported by indexing, but the submitted C2 atomistic model is not sufficiently established. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied and the run ended without a scientific final response; an independent profile check of the submitted CIF gives a large residual (about 0.32) with major intensity errors, including roughly half the observed intensity at 23.98 and 27.88 degrees and severe underprediction at 30.41 and 37.10 degrees. The trajectory compared several C2/m, C2, Cm, and Ci parameterizations using custom stick/amplitude objectives, but its best low residual C2 basins were rejected for impossible contacts, and the final contact-constrained C2 realization remained a visibly inferior compromise; K/Ca ordering and the exact symmetry/coordinates were not independently resolved. A materially different, chemically valid model on the supported lattice could plausibly improve the candidate set, so another solution attempt is warranted.

The primitive hexagonal cell (a about 3.8742 A, c about 6.8530 A), Z=2, and the average ZrBeSi-like framework are strongly supported by the reflection positions, and the Li-on-2a assignment is favored over the tested high-symmetry site permutations. The submitted Fm-3m model is sufficiently established. Its a = 11.1839 A F-centered cubic cell accounts for essentially the complete observed reflection sequence (the trace reports mean/max peak-position errors of 0.00493/0.0174 degrees), while refinement of the sole free Ga coordinate gives x = 0.19533 and reproduces the extracted intensities very closely across the pattern. The trace instantiated and scored the relevant 56-atom cubic Wyckoff decompositions, including alternative Y-site realizations, and they fit substantially worse; the exact-composition database structure it found has a materially incompatible lattice and is not competitive. Although no comparable Rwp report was supplied, the position, intensity, whole-profile, and physical evidence together leave no scientifically motivated materially different candidate likely to improve the set.

The attempt gives credible support for the approximately 5.611 x 7.856 x 5.550 A, 244.68 A^3 perovskite-derived cell and Z=1, and the submitted model is stoichiometric with plausible Fe-O distances. It does not establish exact recovery, however. No external comparable Rwp is available; the trace's final unweighted whole-profile Rwp is about 5.48%, versus an estimated noise floor of about 2.57%, with systematic intensity errors (especially low-angle peaks). More importantly, the claimed P1 structure was not solved as a general P1 model: its coordinates remain constrained to relations inherited from a transformed Pnma parent while only a few parent coordinates and the triclinic metric were refined. The small angular deviations from 90 degrees therefore support, at most, possible metric lowering, not the submitted P1 symmetry and 20 exact independent coordinates. Sr placement was compared only among four sites of that fixed framework, and other symmetry-lowered coordinate relaxations or materially different A-site-ordering realizations were not instantiated. Thus the cell and average framework are promising, but the symmetry, coordinates, and discrete ordering are insufficiently resolved, so another solution attempt is warranted.

The sharp pattern strongly supports the indexed I-tetragonal cell, but not the submitted exact structure. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and validation relied on a 0.952 stick-intensity cosine; a convolved-profile check still gives a large normalized residual of about 0.30 and the model predicts material unmatched reflections. The CIF is a 60-atom P1 realization with exact centering but no established higher symmetry. In the trace, the proposed I41/acd model failed, after which one flexible low-symmetry charge-flip realization was refined without a convincing comparison of distinct symmetries or element orderings. Its irregular coordination and short contacts (including S-S/S-Cl near 1.88-1.89 angstrom and short cation-cation contacts) further weaken physical plausibility. Thus the cell and perhaps average framework are supported, while symmetry, coordinates, and ordering remain materially unresolved and another solution attempt is warranted.

The tetragonal cell (a approximately 10.167 A, c approximately 4.764 A), body centering, Z=8, and the average Cu-S/Li framework are well supported, and the submitted distances are chemically plausible. Exact recovery is not sufficiently established: no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied; the submitted model retains systematic intensity mismatches (an independent simple profile convolution gives about 9% unweighted Rwp); its own whole-profile refinement favored different coordinates, especially Li; and the trajectory's subgroup searches generally forced one multiplicity-8 orbit per element rather than instantiating the split-orbit realizations needed to compare the I4/mmm model fairly with lower-symmetry same-cell structures. A locally relaxed I-4 realization already reduced the trajectory's intensity objective, while Li is too weakly scattering for the selected Li coordinate/order to be treated as uniquely resolved. A further attempt that performs comparable whole-pattern refinements of the parent and properly instantiated subgroup/split-site alternatives is scientifically warranted.

The primitive triclinic cell is strongly supported by peak positions (19/20 indexed lines, M(19)=133.2), and its volume makes Z=1 plausible, but this does not establish the submitted P-1 symmetry or atomistic realization. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied; an independent flexible profile check of selected.cif still gave an unweighted residual of about 0.262, and the trajectory's explicit profile refinements were also poor (best reported Rwp about 0.367). The final coordinates were instead selected with a custom extracted-line-intensity objective plus ad hoc distance penalties, after the trace acknowledged several similarly fitting mathematical oxygen solutions; materially different solutions were not instantiated as CIFs and compared. Physical plausibility is also inadequate: the model has V-O contacts down to 1.499 A, many O-O contacts near 2.15 A, and grossly inconsistent V bond-valence environments (representative V(V)-parameter sums about 2.13, 6.45, and 5.80; automated valence assignment fails). Thus the cell/average scattering framework may be credible, but the submitted symmetry, coordinates, and oxygen arrangement are not sufficiently established, and another scientifically motivated solution/refinement attempt is warranted.

The primitive trigonal cell, Z = 1, A-site-layered perovskite average framework, and placement of Fe on the octahedral sublattice are strongly supported by the peak positions and the good approximate intensity match. However, exact recovery of the submitted P3m1 realization is not sufficiently established. The trajectory instantiated only one ideal, undistorted [111] perovskite geometry with all coordinates fixed at special rational values and compared cation permutations on those fixed sites; it did not refine or compare symmetry-lowered/distorted coordinate models, occupancies, or physically motivated alternatives. Its six nominal Ba/La/Mg layer permutations gave identical scores, and the reported 0.00118 degree metric is only a peak-position RMS, not a whole-pattern structural score; the comparable Rwp report is unavailable. The ideal model is also chemically strained by placing Mg in the large 12-coordinate A cavity. Thus the cell and average framework may be right while the submitted symmetry and exact coordinates remain underdetermined, and another attempt focused on whole-pattern refinement and distorted/lower-symmetry variants is warranted.

The tetragonal metric and average B/C-layer framework are well supported by the peak positions and the custom profile fit, but exact recovery is not sufficiently established. DICVOL's strongest solution was the half-volume tetragonal cell (a about 3.80 A, c about 3.761 A, V about 54.3 A^3, consistent with Z=1), yet the trajectory did not instantiate or intensity-fit any structure in that cell; it instead imposed a doubled a about 5.374 A, Z=2 P4/mbm prototype. The calculated reflections that distinguish the doubled cell are extremely weak and are not resolved above the observed noise, so the submitted symmetry, periodic B/C ordering, and associated coordinates are not independently supported by the diffraction data. The only declared alternative is a B/C exchange within the same imposed framework, and no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied. A half-cell realization or another ordering/lower-symmetry model is therefore a materially different, physically plausible survivor that warrants another solution attempt.

The trace establishes a C-centered monoclinic cell near a=6.7844, b=7.4157, c=6.4012 A, beta=92.716 degrees and makes Z=4 plausible, but it does not establish exact recovery of the submitted C2 structure. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp is available, and the optimization used a custom reflection-intensity objective rather than a validated full-profile refinement. The final calculated intensities retain large mismatches (for example, observed/calculated values in the trace are about 39.8/17.5 at 23.98 degrees, 32.6/14.7 at 27.88 degrees, 20.4/35.0 at 35.87 degrees, and 6.9/15.9 at 41.55 degrees), along with predicted intensity at weak or absent lines. The submitted CIF also retains b=7.42418 A even though the trace's corrected metric refinement gives b=7.41573 A. Although the carbonate geometry is plausible, short K-O/K-F, Ca-O/Ca-F, K-Ca, F-O, and O-O contacts indicate a strained packing. Most importantly, the trajectory found many distinct minima and did not adequately resolve or retain competing symmetry/coordinate realizations or the weakly X-ray-distinguishable K/Ca site-ordering ambiguity. Thus the cell and broad framework are better supported than the submitted symmetry, coordinates, and element ordering, and another scientifically motivated solution attempt is warranted.

The primary CIF is valid and expands in the primitive P6_3/mmc cell (a=b=3.87420 A, c=6.85300 A, alpha=beta=90 degrees, gamma=120 degrees, V=89.079 A^3) to six fully occupied, ordered atoms, Li2Cu2S2 (Z=2; reduced LiCuS), with Li 2a, Cu 2c, and S 2d. All reproducible reflections from 25.98 to 88.02 degrees are indexed (the calculated 74.76/74.81-degree pair is observed as one overlap), the cell fit has about 0.0011-degree position RMS, and the apparent 47.11-degree excursion is not a coherent peak above the decaying neighboring tail. The trace contains an auditable integrated-intensity comparison of the instantiated model across the observed lines: it strongly rejects putting Cu or S on 2a; swapping Cu and S between 2c and 2d is only an origin-shift-equivalent setting; and releasing the coordinates in P6_3mc repeatedly gives only a negligible fit improvement, not a supported distinct realization. Periodic chemistry has no overlaps, gives trigonal Cu-S contacts of 2.237 A and complete Li neighbor shells at 2.818 A, and bond-valence analysis supports charge-balanced Li(+1)/Cu(+1)/S(-2). Thus the missing separate comparable Rwp does not outweigh the trace's line-coverage and atomic-intensity evidence, and no concrete viable diffraction-relevant branch remains absent from the submitted set.

The submitted CIF is a valid, explicit ordered realization: it parses and symmetry-expands in Fm-3m (No. 225) to full-occupancy Y8Ga48 (YGa6, 56 atoms, Z=8) with a=11.1839 A; primitive standardization gives Y2Ga12 (14 atoms), so equivalent cell settings do not create a distinct structure. All 34 substantive extracted reflections are indexed by the cubic lattice with about 0.0032 degrees peak-position RMSE and no important unexplained line. Direct comparison of the instantiated CIF gives an independently integrated-intensity RMS residual of 1.79% (absolute R=2.54%); a constrained whole-profile fit refines the Ga 24e coordinate back to x=0.19530 and has Rprofile=8.57%, only 0.19 percentage points above a free-intensity Pawley-like lower bound (8.38%). Independent height- and area-based refinements converge near x=0.19533, while the tested 48h-only and Y-on-4a+4b orderings fit far worse. Periodic chemistry is valid, with no overlaps (shortest Y-Ga 2.796 A and Ga-Ga 2.862 A), complete plausible neighbor shells, correct stoichiometry, and no meaningful ionic charge-balance contradiction for this intermetallic. Lower-symmetry indexings that miss reflections and lack an instantiated competitive intensity fit are not concrete surviving branches.

The submitted CIF is a valid, fully occupied, ordered primitive P3m1 (No. 156) realization: symmetry expansion gives exactly Ba1La1Mg1Fe3O9 in 15 atoms, Z=1, with a=b=5.52885 A, c=6.74035 A, gamma=120 degrees and V=178.4361 A^3; primitive standardization does not reduce it further. Every substantive observed reflection is indexed (31 reliable line centers have 0.00118 degrees 2theta RMS error, and no unmatched peak has prominence above about 10 times the baseline noise). The instantiated structure also has atom-coordinate intensity support: the trace compares 38 resolved/semi-resolved reflections and obtains robust log-intensity RMS 0.1106 after only scale and smooth Q attenuation, while the next inequivalent cation-site partitions are at least 0.4879; an independent common-profile whole-pattern check is close to its free-intensity lower bound (about 4.2% versus 3.5% unweighted residual). The six apparent Ba/La/Mg layer permutations reduce to the same periodic structure, whereas placing Ba, La, or Mg on the Fe octahedral sublattice is quantitatively rejected. Periodic shells contain no overlaps (Fe-O=1.952 A in complete FeO6 octahedra; each A site has the complete 12-O shell at 2.756-2.764 A), and Ba2+/La3+/Mg2+/Fe3+/Fe4+/Fe4+/O2- is charge balanced. The unusual long Mg-O A-site environment is not, by itself, a concrete diffraction-compatible alternative. Thus the set already contains an explicit supported realization and no material surviving discrete branch is identifiable.

The primary CIF parses and symmetry-expands in primitive P4/mbm (No. 127) to a fully occupied 10-atom Ce2B4C4 cell (reduced Ce(BC)2, Z=2) with a=b=5.373745 A, c=3.761059 A and V=108.6086 A^3; primitive standardization does not reveal a distinct reduced structure. All 22 material observed reflections are indexed without an important unexplained line (0.00483 degree 2theta RMS, 0.01282 degree maximum). More decisively, an independently reproduced whole-profile fit of the fixed instantiated primary CIF gives 0.15869 intensity-unit RMS (unweighted profile ratio 0.0371), close to the independent-intensity profile lower bound of 0.15160; extracted and CIF-calculated integrated intensities correlate at 0.99989 with only 1.27% relative L2 discrepancy. In the trace, incompatible B/C layer placements give much poorer 0.82-1.89 RMS fits, whereas the B/C-exchanged ordering remains essentially tied (0.15896 RMS) and is explicitly supplied as alternative-1.cif. Both submitted orderings are compositionally valid and distinct, and complete periodic-neighbor checks find no overlap or pervasive impossible bonding (primary minimum distance 1.547 A, B-C 1.547-1.598 A, Ce shell 8 C at 2.759 A plus 8 B at 2.809 A). Thus an explicit ordered realization has convergent coordinate-level diffraction support and passes validity and chemistry checks, while the credible surviving ordering ambiguity is covered; no concrete incompatible viable branch remains.

The submitted CIF is parseable and explicitly ordered: it symmetry-expands in C2 (No. 5) to 28 fully occupied atoms, K4Ca4C4O12F4 (Z=4), and primitive-standardizes to 14 atoms (Z=2). It is charge-balanced and has intact carbonate groups (C-O 1.284-1.286 A) without a gross overlap veto. Indexing is strong (21/21 selected lines, M(20)=110.9), but the atomic structure is not established. No comparable Rwp was supplied, and the trace's instantiated-CIF intensity comparison remains far above the pattern noise and contains major errors, including observed/calculated intensities of 39.82/17.48 for 020, 32.58/14.68 for 002, 20.39/34.95 for 220, 4.40/0.06 near 30.41 degrees, and 1.29/7.62 near 44.84 degrees; the final optimization still reported an approximately 0.154 intensity-residual component. Independent searches did not converge to this coordinate set, and the run itself rejected earlier numerical minima as chemically impossible or conventionally intensity-incompatible. Moreover, the submitted b=7.42418 A was retained after the trace discovered an erroneous monoclinic d-spacing expression; the corrected indexing fit gave b=7.41573 A, leaving avoidable peak-position offsets in the actual CIF. Thus good indexing does not rescue the dubious atomic-intensity fit, and another attempt is likely to produce a materially different viable realization.

decision.reason: The monoclinic cell is strongly supported by indexing (all first 20 peaks indexed; M(20)=61.8), and C-centering/c-glide absences give useful support for a C2/c average framework, but the submitted exact realization is not sufficiently established. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the trajectory's own final constrained-profile fit has data RMS about 1.85 intensity units while the measured background noise is about 0.10, indicating substantial intensity mismatch despite plausible bond distances. The search imposed one C2/c topology with Er on 4e, K on a screened special site, and a single rigid/general carbonate orbit; repeated starts only tested orientation minima within that topology. It did not instantiate and compare lower-symmetry coordinate/order variants or other materially different framework realizations. Thus the cell and broad topology are better supported than the claimed symmetry-exact coordinates and site assignment, and another scientifically motivated solution attempt could plausibly improve the candidate set.

The indexing and profile agreement strongly support the approximately 75.12 A^3, Z=1 cell and an alternating Li/transition-metal ordered-rocksalt average framework, but they do not establish exact recovery of the submitted P2/m realization. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the trajectory constrained the oxygen refinement to P2/m without a quantitative comparison to symmetry/order alternatives. Most importantly, its claim that V/Cr swaps are equivalent was based on the ideal oxygen model: for the submitted distorted coordinates, swapping V and Cr gives a crystallographically distinct, chemically plausible structure whose calculated Cu Kalpha intensities differ by only about 0.1% in aggregate (maximum normalized peak change about 0.072 on a 100 scale), below the pattern noise. Thus the V/Cr ordering, and consequently the site-specific oxygen coordinates, remain a material unresolved discrete ambiguity warranting another attempt.

The candidate set is sufficiently established. The hexagonal cell and Z=3 ordered-antifluorite framework are strongly fixed by the full indexed peak sequence, and the ideal element-specific model reproduces both the major reflections and numerous weak Si/Ge-ordering reflections with no materially unexplained peak family. The 27-atom, full-occupancy structures are compositionally and geometrically plausible (minimum periodic distance about 2.77 A). Crucially, the trajectory explicitly enumerated all 84 choices of three Si sites among the nine framework-anion sites, compared their powder fingerprints, and retained representatives of every best-fitting distinct survivor: the P3_112/P3_212 enantiomorphic pair and the genuinely distinct homometric Immm ordering. Thus the unresolved discrete ordering/symmetry ambiguity is covered rather than hidden in an averaged model. Although no comparable Rwp score was supplied and the CIFs are serialized in P1, round-trip analysis recovers the claimed symmetries from their explicit coordinates, so these caveats do not identify a scientifically motivated materially different candidate likely to improve the set.

The submission is sufficiently established. The primitive monoclinic Z=2 cell is exceptionally well supported (all 20 indexing lines matched, M20 about 260), and the P2/c Li3SbO4-type realization accounts for the clean whole pattern with a reported profile Rwp of about 4.24% and no material unmatched reflections. The refinement improves substantially over the unrefined isotype, while the full-occupancy Li3BiO4 model has plausible density and Bi-O/Li-O coordination. Although the supplied comparable-score report is unavailable and the trajectory did not broadly enumerate unrelated topologies, the diffraction evidence supports the P2/c symmetry and refined framework; obvious discrete Li-site permutations and stoichiometric Li/O site-ordering alternatives fit much worse. No scientifically motivated, materially different surviving candidate is evident that warrants another attempt.

The primitive hexagonal cell (a about 4.086 A, c about 15.584 A), Z=1, and an average layered scattering framework are well supported, but exact structure recovery is not. The quoted 4.6% is a bespoke unweighted 'Rwp-like' residual rather than a comparable whole-pattern score (the supplied report says no such score is available), and meaningful intensity mismatches remain. More importantly, the trajectory only exhaustively compared a tightly restricted P-3m1 model with Hg/Sn fixed on the two onefold sites, Ag on one inversion pair, and Se on two inversion pairs; the lower-symmetry searches were sparse and did not systematically test alternative orderings, occupancies, or symmetry-related discrete ambiguities. The selected ordering is also physically suspect: its own validation finds no Hg-Se neighbor within 4 A, only Hg-Ag contacts near 2.83 A, while Sn is six-coordinate to Se at about 2.80 A. Thus the cell and average electron-density arrangement do not establish the submitted P-3m1 symmetry, coordinates, and element ordering, and a chemically motivated lower-symmetry or differently ordered model could plausibly improve the candidate set.

The hexagonal cell and the Mn5Si3-type average framework are strongly supported: all first 21 peaks index with M20 = 114.7, the submitted model is geometrically plausible, and an independent profile check reproduces the reported approximately 4.2% residual. However, exact recovery is not established. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied, and the trajectory instantiated only the ordered P63/mcm prototype; it did not materialize or compare symmetry-lowered Sn/Sb orderings. With Cu Kalpha radiation, Sn and Sb have very weak scattering contrast. Enumerating the 28 placements of two Sb atoms over the eight submitted Sn/Sb positions at fixed framework coordinates gives many physically plausible ordered realizations with essentially indistinguishable fits (R-like differences only about 0.0002, with the submitted 2b/2b ordering not preferred). Thus the cell, Z = 2, and average framework are supported, but the submitted symmetry and element ordering remain a material unresolved discrete ambiguity warranting another attempt.

The face-centered cubic cell (a about 7.7862 A) and Z=4 are strongly supported by the peak positions, and the imposed F-43m average model reproduces the extracted intensities reasonably well. However, exact recovery is not established: no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the reported profile fit was a custom masked/unweighted fit restricted to an assumed F-lattice/F-43m parameterization rather than a discriminating comparison against materially different coordinate and subgroup models. Most importantly, the submitted coordinates give chemically untenable Ni-Se contacts as short as 1.368 A (with other Ni-Se nearest distances near 2.004 and 3.188 A), a problem the trajectory calculated but did not resolve; the intensity refinement also required a negative B factor. Thus support for the cell and average cubic framework does not establish the submitted symmetry and coordinates, and another scientifically motivated solution attempt is warranted.

The primitive monoclinic cell, Z=1, Li/TM-layered rocksalt framework, and plausible octahedral geometry are well supported, but the exact submitted realization is not. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied, and the trajectory's own fixed-structure profile residual (RMS 0.1634) exceeds its noise-region RMS (0.1037). More importantly, it instantiated only one fully ordered V/Cr P2/m assignment and did not compare V/Cr disorder or materially different periodic orderings before claiming the ordering was resolved. An independent verifier check finds the submitted ordered model and a 50:50 V/Cr-averaged model essentially indistinguishable (unweighted profile RMS 0.15452 versus 0.15468); reflections unique to the proposed V/Cr order are at most about 0.1% of the strongest peak. The oxygen-site split was also unstable and was collapsed to a convenient pseudo-centered realization. Therefore the data strongly support the cell and average framework but do not sufficiently establish the submitted symmetry-breaking V/Cr order, exact oxygen coordinates, or occupancies, so another attempt is warranted to test and materialize the surviving ordering/occupancy alternatives.

The submitted model is sufficiently established. One tetragonal cell indexes all credible reflections across the measured range with an approximately 0.0021 degree 2theta position RMS, and the three fully occupied Y face-center sites reproduce the observed stick-intensity pattern with correlation 0.9973. Crucially, the repeated roughly 9:1 corrected intensity contrast between all-same-parity and mixed-parity reflections is direct support for this three-site basis, not merely for the cell or Z. Because the composition is elemental Y, there is no unresolved element-ordering ambiguity; the exact special-position coordinates have P4/mmm as their detected maximal symmetry and the CIF round-trips correctly. The shortest Y-Y distance (about 3.36 angstrom) and density (about 3.82 g/cm3) are physically plausible, and no credible unindexed peaks or materially distinct surviving structure is evident. The absence of a comparable Rwp is a limitation, but it does not outweigh the strong position and intensity evidence here.

The tetragonal cell (a about 5.714 A, c about 15.817 A, Z=2) and an average filled-U3Si-derived framework are reasonably supported, but exact recovery is not. No comparable whole-pattern score was supplied, and the trace's final fixed-carbon fits have an unweighted profile residual of about 10.87%, versus an estimated noise-limited floor near 3.6%; several weak reflections are substantially missed or mis-scaled. The submitted Hf/Ti-swapped alternative is marginally better by the trace's own residual (0.108653 versus 0.108680), so selection and elemental ordering are unresolved. More importantly, the search instantiated and refined essentially one P4/m prototype realization plus the global Hf/Ti swap, although its discrete enumeration produced multiple intensity-degenerate vacancy/order arrangements; lower-symmetry derivatives and those surviving arrangements were not carried through comparable full-profile refinement. The P4/m-expanded P1 CIFs are compositionally valid and broadly plausible, but the selected model also has a short Ru-C contact of about 1.74 A. A further attempt that explicitly compares the remaining vacancy/order variants and lower-symmetry coordinate models is scientifically warranted and could materially improve the candidate set.

The monoclinic cell is strongly established and Z=4 is chemically plausible, but the exact submitted structure is not. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied; an independent profile refit of the CIF (optimizing width, zero shift, scale, background, and overall intensity damping) gives an unweighted Rwp of about 42.7% and large major-peak intensity errors, so the diffraction fit is dubious despite sensible carbonate and cation-oxygen geometry. The trajectory searched mainly within a preselected C2/c model with Er on 4e, K on a fixed fourfold site, and one rigid general-position carbonate, and its physically constrained final model fit worse than discarded intensity minima. It did not adequately compare lower-symmetry realizations or materially different carbonate/cation arrangements. Thus the cell and average framework have support, but the submitted symmetry, coordinates, and ordering are not sufficiently established, and another solution attempt is warranted.

The peak positions strongly establish the approximately 75.12 A^3 primitive cell (Z=1), and the submitted ordered-rocksalt framework gives a good whole-pattern fit with plausible octahedral distances. However, exact recovery is not established. The trajectory compared cation permutations only on an ideal oxygen sublattice, where multiple alternating Li/V/Cr assignments produced identical calculated patterns, and then refined oxygen coordinates for only one convenient assignment. Once that oxygen relaxation breaks the ideal pseudo-translation, a V/Cr-swapped relaxed realization is a distinct candidate; given the very similar Cu-Kalpha scattering of V and Cr, it was not resolved or fairly compared. The P2/m symmetry and its special-coordinate constraints were likewise imposed without profile comparisons to symmetry-lowered models, and no comparable Rwp score was supplied. Another attempt should explicitly instantiate and jointly refine the surviving V/Cr ordering(s) and reasonable symmetry subgroups before the submitted coordinates and element ordering can be considered sufficiently established.

The hexagonal cell is strongly indexed by all 26 selected lines and the refined metric supports Z=3; the submitted 27-atom models have the correct composition, full occupancies, and plausible ordered-antifluorite geometry (minimum distance about 2.77 A). More importantly, the trajectory instantiated all 84 Si/Ge assignments on the nine anion sites and compared their calculated powder intensities to the observed profile, rather than inferring ordering from the cell alone. The retained fingerprint reproduces the strong parent peaks and weak superstructure peaks nearly line-for-line (reported intensity correlation about 0.99975), with no meaningful unexplained observed peak. Its surviving discrete ambiguity was not averaged away: the distinct centrosymmetric Immm realization and both chiral P3_112/P3_212 realizations are explicit element-specific CIF candidates and were verified to be exactly powder-homometric. Although the CIFs are conservatively serialized in P1 and no standardized comparable Rwp was supplied, symmetry recovery from their coordinates gives the stated groups, and the available peak-position, integrated-intensity, composition, occupancy, and geometry checks make a materially different framework unlikely to improve the candidate set.

The 171.38 A^3 primitive monoclinic cell, Z=2, and the Li3SbO4-type Bi/O average framework are strongly supported by indexing and a good internal profile fit, and the submitted full-occupancy model has plausible density and bond lengths. Exact recovery is not sufficiently established, however: the only structural family actually instantiated was the borrowed P2/c analogue; lower-symmetry or different periodic realizations were not compared, the comparable whole-pattern score is unavailable, and Cu K-alpha data weakly constrain Li. A common-profile check leaves a chemically plausible alternative Li realization essentially indistinguishable (about 4.42% versus 4.43% unweighted residual), while a substantially shifted plausible Li model is still close. Thus the fit mainly establishes the cell and heavy-atom/oxygen framework, not the submitted Li coordinates or uniquely P2/c realization, so another attempt is warranted to instantiate and compare the surviving alternatives.

The peak positions strongly establish the primitive trigonal cell (a about 4.086 A, c about 15.584 A) and are consistent with Z=1 and a layered average framework, but they do not sufficiently establish the submitted element-specific P-3m1 realization. The reported 4.6% value is an ad hoc unweighted Rwp-like metric with no comparable whole-pattern score available; even after profile refinement the RMS residual (about 0.234) exceeds the off-peak noise (about 0.124-0.140) and retains systematic intensity errors. More importantly, the CIF gives Hg no Se neighbors within 4 A (only two Ag neighbors), yields six-coordinate Sn at 2.80 A, and fails to recover the chemically expected Ag(I)/Sn(IV)/Hg(II)/Se(-II) bond-valence assignment. The trajectory's zero chemical penalty tested only short contacts, not bonding plausibility, and its decisive enumeration constrained all atoms to three trigonal axes and inversion-related P-3m1 sites; it did not instantiate and compare off-axis lower-symmetry, ordered-supercell, or other chemically plausible realizations. A materially different model preserving the well-supported cell/average diffraction while restoring plausible Hg-Se and Sn-Se coordination therefore remains scientifically motivated.

The indexed primitive hexagonal cell (a about 10.443 A, c about 7.154 A) and a physically plausible stuffed-Mn5Si3-type average framework are strongly supported, and the submitted model gives a good self-computed profile fit. Exact recovery is not sufficiently established, however: the trajectory instantiated and refined only the prototype-derived P63/mcm realization, the supplied comparable-score report contains no comparisons, and Z = 2 is inherited from that realization rather than independently demonstrated. Most importantly, Cu Kalpha powder data have very weak contrast between adjacent elements Sn and Sb. Composition-preserving enumeration of the eight Sn/Sb framework positions gives 28 fully ordered realizations whose normalized profiles differ from the submission by at most about 0.44%, with several fitting marginally better in an independent common-profile check. Thus the submitted high symmetry and the assignment of both Sb atoms to the 2b axis remain a material unresolved discrete ambiguity; lower-symmetry/order alternatives should be explicitly instantiated and compared in another attempt.

The F-centered cubic cell (a about 7.7862 A) is strongly supported and Z=4 is plausible, and the submitted F-43m average model gives good integrated-intensity agreement when anomalous scattering is included. However, exact recovery is not sufficiently established: no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the reported profile fit is not a conventional independently comparable refinement. More decisively, the model is physically implausible, with one Ni orbit having Ni-Se contacts near 1.37 A while another has its nearest Se near 3.19 A. The trajectory only compared a restricted set of high-symmetry Wyckoff prototypes and origin-equivalent special-site choices; it did not instantiate chemically constrained lower-symmetry, occupancy/disorder, or materially different ordering alternatives. Thus the data support the cubic cell and an average scattering arrangement, but not the submitted exact symmetry, coordinates, full occupancies, and ordering, so another solution attempt is warranted.

The monoclinic 74.51 A^3 cell, Z=1, and the layered Li/transition-metal average framework are strongly supported by the peak positions, and the fixed-model profile fit is broadly good. Exact recovery is not established: no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied; the trace assumed one P2/m cation-ordering topology and did not instantiate or compare distinct V/Cr ordering supercells or other periodic orderings; and the ordering-sensitive reflections of the submitted model are no more than about 0.10% of the strongest calculated line, at or below the observed noise (with the strongest overlapping the basal-peak tail). The trace also adopted pseudo-centered, tied oxygen coordinates because the P2/m-allowed oxygen split was unstable across weighting schemes, so the submitted symmetry-specific coordinates are a convenient average realization rather than a resolved result. With only that one CIF and no alternatives, another attempt is warranted to compare scientifically plausible ordering/symmetry and oxygen-distortion realizations using whole-pattern scores.

The tetragonal cell and parity-dependent intensity modulation are strongly supported, and the submitted full-occupancy three-face-center P4/mmm model fits the observed peak positions and relative intensities well. However, exact Z and occupancies are not established: a materially different P4/mmm realization with Y occupancy 1 at (0,0,0) and 1/3 on each of the same three face-center sites has Z=2 and produces exactly the same reflection positions and normalized whole-pattern intensities (its calculated intensities differ only by a global factor of 4/9). The trace did not instantiate or compare this homometric occupancy branch, instead asserting uniqueness from a peak-height correlation; moreover, no comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied. Because the submitted set therefore resolves the cell/Patterson motif but not the exact occupancy realization, another attempt is warranted.

The tetragonal cell (a about 5.714 A, c about 15.817 A), Z=2, and a U3Si-derived average metal framework are credible, and the final CIFs have the right composition, full occupancies, and no obvious catastrophic final contact. Exact recovery is not established, however. The comparable whole-pattern report is unavailable, while the trace's own chemically constrained refinements reach only Rwp about 0.10865-0.10868 and retain substantial weak- and moderate-line intensity discrepancies. Letting carbon improve the profile produced impossible 0.64-0.74 A Ru-C contacts, showing that the chosen topology cannot absorb the residual physically. The trajectory ultimately refined only one constrained P4/m prototype/vacancy realization and its global Hf/Ti swap; its earlier enumeration contained many tied discrete assignments without a demonstrated equivalence audit, and it did not materially compare lower-symmetry distortions or different chemically plausible carbon/framework realizations. Moreover, the submitted CIFs formally declare P1 although their coordinates are detected as P4/m, and the submitted alternative marginally outfits the selected model. Thus the evidence supports the cell and average framework much more strongly than the submitted symmetry, carbon positions, exact coordinates, and Hf/Ti ordering, so another scientifically motivated attempt is warranted.

The CIF is valid and symmetry-expands in C2/c to a fully occupied K4Er4C8O24 conventional cell (40 atoms, Z=4; 20-atom primitive cell), with intact carbonate groups and no overlaps, and the indexed cell gives strong line-position coverage. However, exact atomic-coordinate recovery is not established by the intensities. No separate comparable score was supplied, and the trace's instantiated final-model fit has profile RMSE about 1.85 while the measured baseline noise is about 0.10 (roughly 19 times noise). Independent recalculation likewise gives Rwp about 43% and major intensity contradictions: for example the model predicts a strong reflection near 36.52 degrees where the observed profile is near background, overpredicts 22.57 degrees, and underpredicts 23.21 and 28.71 degrees. The independent-search claim is also overstated because one constrained 4c start retained a distinct carbonate orientation. Thus the cell/topology may be plausible, but the submitted coordinates are not a sufficiently established exact realization and another structure-solution attempt is likely to add a materially different viable candidate.

decision.proposed_branch: Refine and submit the P2/m realization with V and Cr exchanged between (1/2,0,1/2) and (0,1/2,1/2), allowing the two symmetry-constrained oxygen orbits to refine.
decision.reason: The primary CIF is valid and primitive-standard: P2/m, Z=1, eight fully occupied sites expanding to Li2VCrO4. It has complete significant-line coverage, a chemically sound ordered-rocksalt network with six-coordinate cations and bond-valence-compatible Li(+1)/V(+3)/Cr(+3)/O(-2), and an instantiated whole-profile fit of Rwp about 6.64% versus a Pawley-style bound of about 5.93%. However, the decisive V/Cr ordering is not established. Swapping V and Cr between the two distinct onefold transition-metal sites in the refined oxygen framework is not symmetry-equivalent to the submitted structure; after independent oxygen-coordinate refinement, that explicit P2/m realization remains chemically valid and gives an indistinguishable fit (Rwp 6.6345% versus 6.6356%). The trace's claimed equivalence was tested only for ideal oxygen coordinates, so it does not reject this material exact-structure branch, and no corresponding alternative CIF was submitted.

The primary CIF is valid and explicitly contains 27 fully occupied atoms (Mg18Si3Ge6 = 3 Mg6SiGe2) in the stated 7.840817 x 7.840817 x 11.088589 angstrom, 90/90/120 degree cell; although encoded in P1, coordinate symmetry recovery gives P3_112 (No. 151) with the claimed ordering. Indexing covers all 26 selected lines, and an independent coverage check found every observed peak above 5 sigma within 1.2 fitted profile widths of a CIF reflection with no important unexplained peak. The instantiated CIF gives integrated-intensity correlation 0.9997 and R(abs) about 6.4%; its constrained whole-profile unit-weight Rwp is 10.7% versus 10.4% for a same-position/profile Pawley-like lower bound, so the residual is profile-limited rather than evidence against the atomic model. Enumeration of all 1:2 Si/Ge orderings yields only three powder fingerprints: the submitted homometric family is best, while the Cm and P-3m1 fingerprints worsen Rwp to about 11.9% and 18.4% and are quantitatively rejected. The explicit P3_212 enantiomorph and distinct Immm homometric ordering are both submitted. All CIFs parse and round-trip; the primary has no overlaps (minimum periodic distance 2.772 angstrom), complete antifluorite shells (each Si/Ge has eight Mg at 2.772 angstrom and each Mg has four anion neighbors), full occupancies, and charge-balanced Mg(II)/Si,Ge(-IV) stoichiometry. No concrete viable diffraction-incompatible realization remains absent from the submitted set.

The primary CIF parses without warnings and symmetry-expands in primitive P2/c (No. 13) to 16 fully occupied ordered atoms, Li6Bi2O8 = 2(Li3BiO4), with the stated 171.3772 A^3 cell and no hidden supercell or Z discrepancy. Indexing covers all 20 test lines, and independent verification finds every observed peak above intensity 1 within 0.04 degrees of a calculated CIF reflection and no calculated peak above 0.5 lacking observed signal. More decisively, an independently refitted whole profile from the instantiated CIF gives Rwp 4.25%, close to a fixed-cell/shape Pawley free-intensity lower bound of 3.89%; the trace also documents converged coordinate and cell/profile refinements. The cation ordering is resolved: moving Bi onto the three Li orbits worsens comparable whole-profile Rwp to 7.40%, 37.37%, or 56.87%. The model is charge-balanced as Li(+1)3Bi(+5)O4(-2), has six-coordinate Li-O and Bi-O shells (minimum contacts 2.071 and 2.081 A), no overlaps, and bond-valence analysis supports Li(+1)/Bi(+5)/O(-2); the unscaled sums are somewhat underbonded for Li but not a demonstrable chemical failure. No important unexplained reflection, incompatible occupancy/framework, or concrete symmetry-lowered or alternative ordered realization survives, so another attempt is unlikely to add a materially different viable candidate.

The submitted CIF is valid and symmetry-expands in primitive P-3m1 (No. 164) to exactly eight fully occupied atoms, Ag2SnHgSe4 with Z=1, a=4.08605 A and c=15.58409 A; standardization finds no smaller cell. All 32 selected strong reflections index in this cell with mean 2theta error about 0.0012 degrees and no important unindexed line, while the instantiated ordered model was refined against integrated intensities and the complete 5-90 degree profile, giving an integrated-intensity objective near 0.004 and an all-point relative profile residual near 4.6%. Exhaustive P-3m1 site-assignment tests place Sn at 1a, Hg at 1b, Ag on 2e, and Se on the two 2d pairs; the equivalent best solutions collapse to the same realization, whereas the nearest distinct assignment scores about 0.092 (over twenty times worse), and independent lower-symmetry searches did not produce a competitive branch. Periodic checks show no overlaps (shortest contacts are Ag-Se at 2.499 A), the nominal composition is charge-balanced, and complete shells reveal unusual but not demonstrably impossible Ag-Hg/Sn-Se coordination. No concrete incompatible realization remains supported by the blind diffraction evidence.

The submitted CIF is valid and strongly supports the parent framework: it parses and symmetry-expands in P63/mcm to a primitive 18-atom Zr10Sn6Sb2 cell (Zr5Sn3Sb, Z=2) with unit occupancies, the stated cell, a 3.266 A minimum periodic separation, and plausible complete neighbor shells. All 64 observed maxima with prominence above 1 are matched within 0.016 degrees, and an independently reproduced instantiated-model whole-profile fit gives Rwp 4.12%, close to a fixed-cell unconstrained-intensity lower bound of 3.89%. However, the exact Sn/Sb ordering is not established. A concrete fully ordered subgroup realization made by putting Sn on the two parent 2b sites and Sb on a two-site subset of the parent Sn 6g orbit (for example fractional sites 0.394239,0.394239,0.25 and 0.605761,0.605761,0.75) retains the same cell, composition, atom count, coordinates, distances, and viable topology; it symmetry-detects as Cmcm and gives a directly comparable Rwp of 4.10%, slightly better than the submitted model. Its strongest newly allowed distinct reflection is only about 0.0012% of the pattern maximum, so the observed absences do not reject it. Because Sn and Sb have nearly indistinguishable Cu-Kalpha scattering and the trace neither instantiated nor quantitatively rejected this material ordering/symmetry-lowering branch, another attempt is likely to add a materially different viable exact-structure candidate.

The primary CIF parses and standardizes correctly: it contains 28 fully occupied atoms (Ni12Se16, Z=4) in a=7.78618 A cubic symmetry recovered as F-43m No. 216, with a 7-atom primitive Ni3Se4 cell. Indexing is strong (all 15 significant lines match the F-cubic sequence within 0.013 degrees), and an independent anomalous-scattering comparison of integrated intensities from the instantiated CIF reproduces the trace's good fit (R_area about 1.65%). Nevertheless, the ordered realization fails a decisive periodic-chemistry check: every Ni on the recovered 4c orbit has four Se neighbors at only 1.369 A, and every Se participates in one such Ni-Se contact; the 4a Ni orbit instead has its first Se shell at 3.188 A. This is a pervasive atomic overlap, not a cutoff-based coordination preference. The trace itself calculated the same approximately 1.368 A contacts before finalization but neither repaired them nor supplied a chemically valid alternative. Therefore the low diffraction residual does not sufficiently establish this exact structure, and another attempt is required to find a non-overlapping atomic realization compatible with the indexed F-cubic pattern and intensities.

The submitted CIF is valid and sufficiently established. It parses without warnings and symmetry-expands in a primitive P2/m cell (a=5.1313, b=2.9665, c=5.2063 A, beta=109.914 deg, V=74.5115 A^3, Z=1) to 8 fully occupied atoms with composition Li2VCrO4.
